V 2.17.5 [03-08-2026]
    - Minor refactoring for dealing with the thread safety of process requiring the loading of shared tables (e.g. Death Matrix)
V 2.17.4 [23-07-2026]
    - Added the new RLO stability criteria (qcrit_betadep) from the paper Echeveste+26: https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2026arXiv260630303E/abstract
V 2.17.3 [03-07-2026]
    - NEW RLO formalim: Added the new RLO formalism tauris_rl. It uses equations 4.58 in the Tauris&VandenHeuvel book (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2023pbse.book.....T/abstract)
                        It only changes the semimajor axis and it neglects the orbital-spin coupling or spin-up and sping-down due to RLO mass transfer.
                        There are new four runtime parameter (rlo_tauris_alfa,rlo_tauris_beta, rlo_tauris_delta, rlo_tauris_gamma) used to set the evolution of the RLO.
    - NEW binary wind formalim:   Added the new wind formalism tauris.   It uses Eq. 4.38 in the Tauris&VandenHeuvel book (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2023pbse.book.....T/abstract).
                        The spin-up due to mass accretion is neglected, the maximum mass accreted is like in the formalism hurleyTT24mode.

V 2.17.1 [27-05-2026]
    - BUG-FIX-1: Fixed a bug on the isotropic sampling of directions for the Disberg25 kicks
    - BUG-FIX-2: Fixed a bug on isotropic sampling of a specif correction of the kicks when the kicks is 0 but the minimum kick is set to >0

V 2.17.0 [08-05-2026]
    - CHANGE:    COWD/ONeWD classification now (really) follows the Hurley+00 criterion (Section 6).
                 The WD type is determined by the helium core mass at the base of the AGB.
                 (M_{c,BAGB}): COWD if M_{c,BAGB} < 1.6 Msun, ONeWD otherwise.
                  The base of the AGB is identified with the start of the SHeBurning phase.
                        An auxiliary star is initialised at that phase to retrieve the core mass
                        from the interpolating track.

V 2.16.1 [29-04-2026]
    - **Bug fix:** the  version  2.16.0 introduced a small bug in which during the WD formation a pointer was never freed producing a minor memory leak. This has been fixed. 

V 2.16.0 [20-04-2026] (small typo correction still using the version 2.16.0
    - Correct a typo in the parameter name eddington_factor.

V 2.16.0 [17-04-2026]
    - NEW: Introducing the folder apps, which contains alternative executables for specific tasks.
           In principle this could become a folder storing community codes and sevnB will be just one of them.
    - NEW: Introduced a new stellar property Reff (effective stellar radius).
           By default, Reff is equal to the stellar radius. If the star is undergoing Roche-Lobe Overflow (RLO),
           Reff is set to the Roche-Lobe radius (or slightly larger than the core radius if the Roche-Lobe
           lies inside the core). In almost all processes and property calculations, the stellar radius has been
           replaced with Reff, ensuring full self-consistency regardless of whether a process is defined in terms
           of angular momentum variations (dJ) or angular velocity variations (dOmega).
           A runtime parameter use_always_Reff has been introduced:
             - If use_always_Reff = True, SEVN will always use Reff.
             - If use_always_Reff = False, SEVN will continue to use the stellar radius instead.
           NOTICE: These updates are still under testing. To use this feature, always call the star methods
           get_Reff() and getp_0_Reff() rather than accessing the Reff property directly.
    - FIX: Fixed a minor bug on the timestep. In the previous version after a timestep smaller
           than TINY, the next timestep is set to 1E-7 to avoid being stuck on very small timesteps
           (this timestep can be anyway modified and rejected by the adaptive timestep). This created
           a problem when the amount of time before the simulation end is smaller than that value
           (either because of user ending time input or because we are close to the ending time).
           Now this value is the minimum between 1E-7 and half the remaining time to end the simulation.
    - FIX: Changed find with rfind in get_absolute_SEVN_path.
           This solves a problem in localising the right path if SEVN is inside nested folders in which
           some parent folder already contains a /src/ folder.
           With rfind we just get the last /src/ that should be the right one.
    - FIX: Changed the default value for the parameter sn_kick_velocity_stdev from 265 km/s (as in Hobbs+05) to
           217 km/s (as in Disberg&Mandel25, https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2025ApJ...989L...8D/abstract).
           In Disberg&Mandel25, they show that the 265 km/s was likely due to an error in the analysis of the data
           in Hobbs+05 (a missing Jacobian when working in the log-space).
    - FIX: Fixed a behaviour that was producing the wrong events when a star was set to swallow because mass fell
           below the threshold of 0.01 Msun. Before the event was set through the process RLOB, but if this happened
           at the beginning of mass transfer it could hide the current RLOB event. Fixed by using the Tides process.
    - FIX: Minor bug fix: set_empty was not doing any action for JIT properties, this caused a bug in which these
           properties are not updated after the formation of a massless remnant. Now the parent JIT class sets V=nan;
           specific properties override this behaviour:
             - Zams, Zmet: do nothing (so that we can recover the properties of the last tracks the object was following)
             - Event, PhaseBSE: just call an evolve so it increases the counter, and the get handles the massless case
    - CHANGE: Introduced the runtime parameter ev_use_track_radius_for_Qconv (default: true). When enabled, the track
              radius is used for the convective-envelope fit used to set the BSE phase 3, mitigating a spurious heating
              effect arising from the new Reff implementation during RLO.
    - CHANGE: Updated CommonEnvelope::special_evolve and CommonEnvelope::main_coalesce for a more self-consistent
              handling of the situation in which a failed CE triggers a Swallow because one star is a compact remnant
              (BH, NS, WD) and the other a star. Now the logfile will report both the MERGER and SWALLOW messages,
              while the BEvent will be 22 (CE_Swallowed).
    - ADDITION: Added the runtime parameter io_logphase_bse. If true, all stellar phases in the logfile are the BSE ones.
    - ADDITION: Added an option (star_rotation) to disable completely the star rotation (always fixed to 0).
    - ADDITION: Change on the JIT property PhaseBSE to allow to call get_0.
    - INTERNAL: Removed outdated python scripts and tutorials.
    - INTERNAL: Added folder to transform output to T0 format (requires documentation).

V 2.15.1 [01-09-2025]
    -     FIX: Fixed a typo in the Phase check when MCO>0 in the custom mass initialisation
               (before an error was raised for a star initialised with MCO>0 in the terminal core helium
                burning phase)
V 2.15.0 [31-08-2025]
    -   COMPATIBILITY: CMAKE is dropping the support for older Cmake version, so now the minimum version for SEVN
                       is the 3.5 (but 3.10 is suggested), please update your version if needed.
	-	FIX: Fixed an issue in the treatment of tides during Roche Lobe Overflow (RLO).
             Previously, an incorrect rescaling of stellar inertia was applied when estimating
             the variation of the stellar angular momentum.
             This resulted in an excessive sink of angular momentum during RLO.
    -  CHANGE:  Improved treatment of Roche Lobe Overflow (RLO) edge cases.
                Specifically, systems where the stellar core radius becomes larger than the orbital semi-major axis are
                now flagged as unstable and forced into a Common Envelope (CE) event.
                This situation is physically unrealistic but indicates an extremely tight binary
                that would inevitably merge. In the standard CE model, these cases correctly end in a merger.
                This modification apply to the standard Hurley RLO options  (hurley, hurley_bse, hurley_rl_propeller,
                 hurleymod).
    - CHANGE:      We removed the restriction on rlo_gamma_angmom > 1. This parameter defines how angular momentum
                       is lost from the system during non-conservative mass transfer in Roche lobe overflow. Previously,
                       due to a misinterpretation, rlo_gamma_angmom was artificially limited to values below 1. However,
                       when modeling angular momentum loss through a circumbinary disc, this parameter represents the
                       ratio sqrt(a_disc / a_binary), where a_disc is the semimajor axis of the circumbinary disc and
                       a_binary that of the binary. For physical consistency, this ratio should generally be larger than 1.
                       Nevertheless, the code does not impose any restriction on using values between 0 and 1.
    - CHANGE:  In the current version, during super-Eddington accretion onto compact remnants or when a nova occurs
               during Roche lobe overflow, the angular momentum loss is no longer automatically set using isotropic
               re-emission as in previous versions. Instead, the value specified by the user through the
               rlo_gamma_angmom option is applied.
    - CHANGE:  In previous versions, swallowing during RLO was forbidden for stars with a core, triggering an error.
               With the new condition (donor RHE > semimajor axis), this case is now allowed and the check has been
               removed.
    - CHANGE:  We slightly relax the check on the spin variation (Spin=Omega/Omega_crit) of stars for binary processes.
               If the initial Spin is <0.1, we allow a maximum variation of 0.1 (before it was 0.01).
               This help in avoiding stalling systems without having a strong impact on the evolution path.
    -  ADDITION: The new RemnantType BWD (Brown Dwarf) has been added. It is intended to represent brown dwarf objects,
                 but at the moment it is only a non-tested prototype. A BWD can appear either by initializing an object
                 from the beginning with the suffix "BWD" in the mass, or by enabling the parameter
                 rlo_allow_browndwarf_formation, in which case it will be produced if, during RLO, a main-sequence
                  donor is stripped below 0.01 Msun, when this happen a BWD log message will appear in the log file.
    -  ADDITION: Added runtime parameter ts_tinydt_binary_fix (default: true).
                 When enabled, this improves the stability and convergence of binary simulations
                 by accepting all steps with timestep < 1e-15 Myr (note: this does not affect
                 the single stellar evolution timestep). Users are encouraged to perform
                 tests to ensure that the fix does not introduce artifacts in
                 their simulations. Previously, this behavior was always applied by default.
	-  ADDITION: Added a new, more flexible constructor for the Star class, allowing custom definitions of stellar mass(es).
                 If the input mass is provided in round parentheses ( .. ),
                 the current total mass and/or core masses can be specified manually for H-stars:
	                 - 2 values (Mzams, Mcurrent): Mzams = ZAMS mass used to select the interpolating track.
	                                               Mcurrent = current stellar mass. Example: (40,20) → Star is
	                                               initialized with the interpolating track
	                                               of a 40 Msun ZAMS star, but its current mass
	                                               is set to 20 Msun (interpolating tracks remain unchanged).
                     - 4 values (Mzams, Mcurrent, MHEcurrent, MCOcurrent): First two values as above.
                                                  MHEcurrent = current He-core mass.
                                                  MCOcurrent = current CO-core mass.
                                                  Example: (40,20,10,0) → Track as for Mzams=40 Msun, but current total
	                                              mass is set to 20 Msun and He-core mass to 10 Msun.
                                                  Note: SEVN checks consistency with the starting time.
                                                  For instance, (40,20,10,0) at ZAMS is invalid since MHE>0 is
                                                  not expected at ZAMS → SEVN returns an error.
                 For pure He stars:
                      - 2 values (MzamsHE, Mcurrent)HE: MzamsHE = initial He-star mass used for track
                      selection on pureHe tables.
	                  Mcurrent = current He-star mass (total mass = He-core mass).
	                  - 3 values (MzamsHE, Mcurrent, MCOcurrent)HE: Same as above, but MCOcurrent sets
	                   the current CO-core mass.
	                   Note: As for H stars, SEVN checks consistency between the input and the evolutionary stage.
	                   If inconsistent, an error is returned.


V 2.14.1 [15-01-2025]
    - Fixed installation files for conda environments setup and readme in the 'installfix' branch:
       1. Removed old conda_senv_env.txt and conda_sevn_python_env_V2.txt files; added new `env_sevn.yaml` and `env_sevnpy.yaml` files
            The old files caused conflict in installation on macOS systems.
            The issue: macOS tried to install packages available only for linux, including compilers, since .txt files linked to linux repositories.
            Fix: Now only the package name is required, without versioning, and will be downloaded from conda-forge repository
            The `compilers` package automatically detects the current system and downloads the correct correspondent compilers.
            Now it is possible to create SEVN and SEVNpy on both linux and macOS systems (both tested), possibly also on Windows (not tested yet).
            Thus, the folder has been renamed just `conda_sevn_environment`.
       2. Updated `Conda environments section` in Readme file with the new terminal line to use to create conda environment from .yaml files
       3. Typo corrected in `Run scripts` Readme section (it prepared for execution the compile.sh instead of the run.sh file)
       4. Bug fixed in the `compile.sh` file that prevented compilation in the correct folders (`..` removed in line 125)
V 2.14.0 [14-01-2025]
    - Introduced a new method to estimate the transition between radiative and convective envelope,
      and thus the transition between the BSE HG and the RGB phase when the convective tables are not available.
      The transition is based on Teff, and the transition temperature from a full radiative to
      fully convective envelope is based on fit made on the PARSEC_ov05 tracks and depend on the mass and metallicity
      of the star.
V 2.13.0 [19-12-2024]
    - Fixed two bugs affecting the evolution of white dwarf (WD) stars:
        1. Moved the accretion check on compact objects to occur after the update of binary evolution properties.
             This ensures that the timestep is correctly checked even if a Type Ia supernova (SN Ia) is triggered.
        2. Fixed an issue in the accretion check that relied only on the current timestep's accretion, rather than
            considering the cumulative accretion over time.
    - Added a new JIT property, `dMcumul_remnant`, to track the cumulative mass accretion on compact remnants
         (black holes [BH], neutron stars [NS], and white dwarfs [WD]).
V 2.12.0 [19-11-2024]
    - Fixed a bug on the method that we use to transform from SEVN phases to BSE types. Due to a typo,
      naked helium stars in the Terminal-Core helium burning phase were assigned to BSE type 7 instead of 8.
V 2.11.2 [10-11-2024]
    -Added the wind mode hurleyTT24mod and set it as the default value.
     This option is a modified version of the Hurley formalism, with the only change being in the maximum accretion
     efficiency. In the original Hurley et al. (2002) version, the maximum accretion efficiency is set to 0.8.
     In this modified version, we instead use the maximum accretion efficiency derived by Tejeda & Toalá (2024) (https://arxiv.org/pdf/2411.01755)
     in the limit of high orbital velocity (where vorb >= vwind).
     The maximum accretion efficiency is equal to m_accretor/Mtotal.
     The maximum accretion efficiency is defined as the ratio m_accretor / M_total.
V 2.11.1 [08-11-2024]
    - Changed the default value of the parameter  runtime rlo_stable_ms from true to false.
      Now the mass transfer for Main Sequence star is not stable by default.
V 2.11.0 [08-11-2024]
    This version introduces a change in the adaptive time-stepping to improve the code's robustness
    against numerical errors. Due to this change, the outputs of older SEVN versions can differ when
    initial same initial conditions are used.
    -  Now, whenever the last timestep is equal to or smaller than a predefined small value (TINY),
       the step is always accepted, and the subsequent timestep is set to a small but manageable value of 1e-7
        (approximately one month). This adjustment improves numerical stability in future steps,
       as the time derivative is estimated using 1e-7 rather than the extremely small value 1e-15,
        which could introduce numerical noise. This modification was prompted by findings that the proposed timestep
        could vary based on system architecture (e.g., ARM CPU on macOS vs. AMD CPU on Linux),
        which we aim to avoid for reproducibility. We tested on ARM CPU on mac os with GNU compiler
        vs Intel CPU on Linux with gcc compiler and Intel CPU on Linux with icc compiler that the compatibility
        of the results is drastically improved (the differences are almost negligible).
    - Additionally, during the activation of the circularization process, the code now checks if eccentricity is zero.
     If it is, the circularization process is skipped, enhancing computational efficiency.
V 2.10.5 [01-11-2024]
    - Added a more robust handling of scol and bcol, now if a star property is included in bcol and viceversa
      an error is raised
V 2.10.4 [24-07-2024]
    - Solved a bug in the implementation of check stalling (before it was not thread safe)
V 2.10.3 [23-07-2024]
    - Added a modification on the EvolveFunctor constructor to be sure that only one instance of the functor is present.
V 2.10.2 [03-07-2024]
    - Changes in the SN model deathmatrix. Now if the Mass of the remnant from the Woosley table
    is within 5% of the preSN mass of the Hecore we flag the event as a direct collapse and the final
    remnant mass is equal to the total preSN mass. This choice is based on the fact that the Woosley
    paper used pureHe simulations, therefore the Mremnant could be underestimate in the case of direct collapse.
V 2.10.1 [24-06-2024]
    - Changed the default wmode to hurley (the old name hurley_wind cannot be used anymore, but the model is the same)
V 2.10.0 [30-05-2024]
    - Changed the standard behaviour of SEVN when the stars  are flagged as WR. Before the star automatically
      jumped to a pureHe track, but we realise this could introduce some minor bias in the stellar evolution.
      We introduce a new runtime parameter turn_WR_to_pureHe so that we can split the flagging from the effect.
      Internally in SEVN a star is still flagged as WR based on the runtime parameter star_tshold_WR_envelope.
      However now a WR flagged star is turned into pureHe just if the parameter turn_WR_to_pureHe is set to True.
      The default is False, so by default a WR flagged star will be jump to pureHe track. In this case,
      a star can jump to pureHe tracks if it completely lose the envelope (based on the runtime parameter ev_naked_tshold).

    - Updated Klencki lambda with a new tables and a new handling of systems with small radius (outside the validity of the fitting equations).
      For star with R<Rtams, the lambda is estimated as lambda(Rtams)*Rtams/R so that the binding energy is constant at the value of the TAMS
       and we avoid spikes at very high values due to the extrapolation of the lambda fitting equations.

V 2.9.0 [23-05-2024]
    - Changes made to improve the stability of the adaptive timestep when also the Star spin is checked.
    - Added the runtime parameter check_stalling_time to set the number of second to wait before to flag
      a system as stalling
    - Now the default evolve functor do not store in the output files the output of the failed files
    - Solved a bug that was not registering the Windaccretion process (just in the V 2.8.1), so this process was not taken into account
V 2.8.1 [16-05-2024]
    - Reintroduced the check for stalling system. Now if a system evolve for more than 20s the systems is considered
    to be stalling, the evolution is stopped and the system is flagged as failed.
V 2.8.0 [16-04-2024]
    - Added the new boolean runtime parameter ns_detailed_accretion to activate the detailed handling of accretion on a NS
       accounting for the change in magnetic field and spin of the NS due to the mass accretion
    - Hurley kicks refactored to avoid to have the kicks internally stored in different units when a BSN kick is triggered.
      Now when getting the SNkick from a class star they are always in units of km/s
V 2.7.7 [15-04-2024]
    - Added the new Roche Lobe overflow model Hurley_rl_propeller, it is the same as Hurley_rl but including
    the propeller mechanism by Campana+18 for accretion on Neutron Stars
